question.text: Activist Cat III funds in India differ from traditional Cat III funds primarily because:

answer.text: They have a LESS diversified portfolio and often hold illiquid investments.
They must have a more diversified portfolio.
They are required to invest 100% in listed securities only.
They are exempt from all concentration limits.

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Section 10.1.4.1: Activist Funds have less diversified portfolios and illiquid investments because they take large stakes to drive operational change. The 10% concentration cap (or 20% for LVFs) binds them to small-mid caps with concentrated positions. **The Trap:** A inverts. C imposes a non-existent rule. D is false — concentration limits absolutely apply (10% or 20% for LVF). **Cross-Exam Context:** XIX-D distressed PE (Cat I/II) is in some ways the Cat I/II cousin but operates differently. XIX-C covers both. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** Illiquid activist positions force side-pocket provisions into the PPM. Pre-draft the side-pocket mechanism trigger (e.g. >25% of NAV in stress-priced securities) so you can invoke it without an LP vote delay.
